findings.title: Recovery codes stored unhashed
findings.body: In `createRecoveryCodesCredential`, the generated recovery codes are serialized to JSON as raw strings (`recoveryCodesJson = JsonSerialization.writeValueAsString(generatedCodes)`) and passed as the credential value to both user storage (`UserCredentialModel`) and local storage (`RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel`). `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils` already provides `hashRawCode`/`verifyRecoveryCodeInput` for hashing codes with `Algorithm.RS512`, but they are not used anywhere in this code path. Anyone with read access to the federated user storage or to the Keycloak DB can read the recovery codes in plaintext and reuse them to bypass 2FA. The codes must be hashed before persistence (e.g., via `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.hashRawCode`) and verified by hashing the user input, as the existing helpers already support.

findings.title: Recovery codes can be reused indefinitely in federated storage
findings.body: `isValid` for `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.TYPE` only does `generatedKeys.stream().anyMatch(key -> key.equals(input.getChallengeResponse()))` and never updates the stored credential data to mark the consumed code. The corresponding local-storage behaviour (see `RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator.isRecoveryAuthnCodeInputValid` which checks `recoveryCodeCredentialModel.allCodesUsed()` and removes the credential) has no counterpart in the user-storage path, so a single recovery code stays valid forever and `allCodesUsed()` will never trigger for federated users.

findings.title: NoSuchElementException when user has no recovery codes
findings.body: `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(user)` returns `Optional<CredentialModel>`, but the constructor immediately calls `credentialModelOpt.get()` and then `recoveryCodeCredentialModel.getNextRecoveryAuthnCode().get().getNumber()`. If the user has no recovery-codes credential (e.g., the authenticator is reached before the credential is created, or the federated storage returns nothing), this throws `NoSuchElementException` and breaks the login form rendering. The constructor should handle the empty Optional (skip rendering, throw a meaningful exception, or the calling site must guard creation).

findings.title: removeStoredCredentialById does not work for federated credentials
findings.body: When all codes are used, the authenticator calls `authenticatedUser.credentialManager().removeStoredCredentialById(recoveryCodeCredentialModel.getId())`. `removeStoredCredentialById` only removes locally stored credentials; for a federated credential (which is exactly the case the PR is enabling) this call is a no-op or an error, so a federated user whose recovery codes are exhausted will never have the credential removed and `allCodesUsed()` will never remove the required action either.

findings.title: disableCredentialType silently ignores recovery-authn-codes
findings.body: `disableCredentialType` only handles OTP types and logs an 'Unsupported to disable credential of type' message for everything else. With the new `supportsCredentialType` accepting `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.TYPE`, an admin call to disable recovery codes for a federated user will silently fail and leave the credential active. The recovery-codes branch must clear `myUser.recoveryCodes` (and likewise `getDisableableCredentialTypesStream` must include the type when present).

findings.title: Federated credential ID is dropped when exposing recovery codes
findings.body: `getCredentials` reconstructs the recovery-codes credential via `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromValues(...)`, which does not set `id` from `myUser.recoveryCodes.getId()`. The credential returned through `getFederatedCredentialsStream()` therefore has a different (likely null) id than the one stored in `myUser.recoveryCodes`. Any caller that subsequently operates on this id (e.g., `removeStoredCredentialById` in `RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator`, or admin REST `DELETE /credentials/{id}`) will target the wrong record. The credential id must be copied into the reconstructed model.

findings.title: getCredentials no longer returns the password credential
findings.body: The new `getCredentials` implementation builds the result list only from `myUser.recoveryCodes` and `myUser.otp`. It never adds `myUser.hashedPassword`. Since the credential manager's federated stream is built from `UserStorageProvider.getCredentials`, the federated user's password will disappear from `getFederatedCredentialsStream()` and from any account/admin REST listing. The pre-existing password handling must be preserved alongside the new recovery-codes entry.

findings.title: Recovery-codes test only covers the happy path
findings.body: `testRecoveryKeysSetupAndLogin` only exercises setup + a single successful login with the first code. It does not verify: an incorrect/wrong-format code is rejected, that a consumed code cannot be reused, that an exhausted credential triggers `CONFIGURE_RECOVERY_AUTHN_CODES` and removes the credential for the federated user, or that recovery codes are not also written to the local DB. Given the data-integrity concerns introduced by this PR (hashing, consumption tracking, removal), at least negative-path and exhaustion assertions are required.

findings.title: Potential NullPointerException on tampered/missing form fields
findings.body: `httpReqParamsMap.getFirst(FIELD_GENERATED_AT_HIDDEN)` and `getFirst(FIELD_GENERATED_RECOVERY_AUTHN_CODES_HIDDEN)` can return `null` (e.g., form tampering or a stale POST). The code then calls `.equals(...)` on the result and `Arrays.asList(generatedCodesString.split(","))` later, both of which throw NPE on null. A null check (or `Objects.equals` with the auth-note value) is needed before the equality test.
